note: fork F3F -- THE FOURTH BASELINE: [config] mode=brokered with NO NETWORK MODULE. The key is `<mode>_nomodule`, derived (not passed) from the `[net] module=none` marker the net arm prints -- see check_arm_order's NOMODULE_RE. This is NOT the `[net] enable=0` shape: enable declines a transport that is here, module=none says there is none (the configuration fork F4 produces when mh_net.dll is missing), and the two lanes differ at the same line with different text. RECORDED FROM THE FIRST NO-MODULE BOOT THAT HAS EVER HAPPENED -- before F3F every graceful-degradation claim about this configuration was a prediction. THE VERDICT THAT AUTHORISED IT (check_arm_order --compare, brokered control -> this run): 2 structural edits, 1 text change, 67 -> 69 lines, and NOTHING ELSE MOVED -- the core arm's sequence is line-for-line the brokered one. The three edits are the three lines below that carry a `why`. Edit ONLY with a --compare verdict in the same commit. EDITED BY fork F4B, twice and both ruled: the module bind's outcome line became step #1 (with the `alt` that makes real absence and a declined load share this file), and the banner at step #26 lost its `([net] module=none)` parenthetical. Both `why` fields carry their --compare verdict.

THE `alt` IS THE POINT HERE: from F4B there are TWO ways to have no transport and they arm IDENTICALLY, so they must select the same baseline. `NOT BOUND` is mh_net.dll genuinely absent from disk (the module_absent suite scenario, and the shape a player can create); `NOT ATTEMPTED` is a run that DECLINED the load with `[net] module=none` (the no_net_boot scenario). Same step, same position, different sentence -- which is exactly what `alt` means in this file. VERDICT (--compare, a pre-F4B module=none run -> each of the two F4B arms): 1 structural edit + 1 text change, 69 -> 70 lines, in both.

This one is libmh.dll -- the 627-TU SPINE, 94.6% of what mh.dll used to be. It sits after mh_net's rather than before it for no deeper reason than that mh_net's line already holds that position in this file; the two modules do not know about each other and neither DllMain does anything, so the order between them is not a contract (mh.c says so). ONE line and not two, for the same reason mh_net's is: the R2 loader-order fact is folded in. lines.why: INSERTED BY fork F4E, and it is the item's ONE ruled baseline edit -- the THIRD member of the class F4A pre-ruled at ruling (b): a satellite bound from DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH costs exactly one structural line at the head of the window. This one is mh_harness.dll, the determinism/replay INSTRUMENT -- seams/harness.cpp, 8.3k lines, which used to be mh.dll's single largest file. VERDICT THAT AUTHORISED IT (check_arm_order --compare, the pre-F4E run of the same mode -> the F4E run): 1 structural edit, 0 text changes, and NOTHING ELSE MOVED -- measured on all four committed templates (brokered 70->71, original 44->45, brokered_nomodule 72->73, config1 40->41). It is ONE line and not two on purpose, the same constraint both sibling binds state: the loader-order fact and the two row counts are folded into this line rather than printed separately, so the bound and absent arms are structurally identical and cost one step each. The row counts (host=27/27 spine=30/30) are the item's own evidence: host rows resolve out of mh.dll and spine rows out of libmh.dll, and `spine=0/30` is Q4's refusal stated in numbers -- configuration (1) with the instrument declining to arm rather than reading invented state. IT GOES LAST OF THE THREE BINDS, and that IS a contract (see mh.c): the instrument is handed libmh's bind verdict as an argument, so it cannot be bound before libmh has been. -- ALT (fork F4E): the same step as read on a lane with NO mh_harness.dll. Absence of the instrument is not a different ARM -- it is the same thirteen shims answering what the un-armed bodies already answered -- so it is an alternative spelling of this step rather than a fifth template. The registered `harness_absent` scenario is the lane that reads it. The `call-through ok` clause is not decoration and is required by tools/check_module_bind.py: GetProcAddress succeeding is not evidence that a CALL across the boundary works, and neither is the module's init returning its ABI (that is a call into the module-level entry, not into the contract). The probe is MH_Harness_WantsPresentTick, chosen for the three reasons MH_Net_IsStarted is one module over -- pure, no side effect, and a KNOWN answer at DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH (0, because load_config has not run).

lines.why: THE BASELINE SELECTOR, and fork F4B's one ruled TEXT CHANGE. Step #26 in every other brokered lane is `; ==== MP transport seams armed ====`; with no module MH_Net_Arm returns before installing anything and prints this instead. Same position, same step -- the four transport install_jmps, the prologue guard, hold_start and the five control-frame handler binds are simply not run. WHAT F4B REMOVED FROM IT: the parenthetical `([net] module=none)`. Until F4B that key was the only way to reach this line; now a missing mh_net.dll reaches it too, and naming one cause in the other's run would be a log that lies. The cause is stated -- loudly, with the full path and the Win32 error -- by the `; [modules] mh_net:` line at the head of this same file, two steps up. One line says WHY, this one says WHAT. check_arm_order's NOMODULE_RE was re-pointed onto the `==== NO NETWORK MODULE` banner in the same commit, which makes the key MORE derived than before: it is now a statement about what the arm DID rather than about a key somebody set.
